sources.entry: CheezyPizza - Send files directly between browsers using WebRTC. No uploads, no cloud storage, and no middleman. Fast, secure, peer-to-peer file sharing. Forked from file.pizza. (Demo, Source Code) BSD-3-Clause Docker

summary.one_liner: CheezyPizza is a browser-based tool that sends files directly between two browsers over WebRTC, with no upload to a server, forked from FilePizza.
summary.what_it_does: CheezyPizza lets a user send files from their browser straight to another person's browser using WebRTC, so the files never pass through a storage server. The uploader keeps the page open and shares a link; downloaders receive the data peer to peer. Each file is hashed with SHA-256 after transfer and verified before it is saved. Files are written incrementally to OPFS or IndexedDB so large transfers do not need to fit in memory, and interrupted downloads can resume from the last saved offset. Multi-file transfers are delivered to the downloader as a zip archive, and transfers can be protected with a password. A Local Share feature uses a websocket server to find and send files to devices on the same network. The README also describes optional Redis for channel metadata and optional TURN/STUN configuration for peers behind NAT.
use_cases: send large files to someone without uploading them to a cloud service
share a file with a colleague via a browser link
transfer files between two devices on the same network
send password-protected files peer to peer
resume an interrupted large file download
self-host a private WebRTC file transfer website
notable: Direct browser-to-browser transfer with no intermediary storage; DTLS-encrypted WebRTC channels
Resumable downloads persisted to OPFS or IndexedDB with automatic reconnect on network change
SHA-256 integrity check before a file is saved, with per-file error isolation in multi-file transfers
Local Share mode for discovering and sending files to devices on the same network
Forked from FilePizza, with the original authors credited
caveats: The uploader's browser window must stay open until the transfer completes
Browser support varies: Safari is marked 'not yet tested', and Brave has limited OPFS and resume support
The README notes TURN support may have limitations due to the maintainer's resources
Default PeerJS and STUN servers are third-party hosts unless self-hosted settings are changed
